title: HookMoE: A learnable performance compensation strategy of Mixture-of-Experts for LLM inference acceleration. Longkai Cheng*, Along He*, Mulin Li, Xueshuo Xie, Tao Li (Nankai Univ., Haihe Lab ITAI, Shenzhen Univ.). EMNLP 2025 main, pp 31594-31606, 4-9 Nov 2025 (ACL Anthology 2025.emnlp-main.1610; PDF text read, 899 lines)
setup: Models (Table 1/3): Mixtral-8x7B (2/8, 46.7B total), Mixtral-8x22B (2/8, 140.6B), Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (14.3B, 64 experts, 4 shared; Table 1 says 8/64 but Table 3 'Origin' is k=4 -- internal inconsistency), DeepSeek-V2-Lite (6 of 64 routed + 2 shared). Method: lower top-k (Mixtral 2->1, Qwen 4->1, DeepSeek 6->3) plus one trainable 2-linear 'Hook' module (0.14-0.70% of params) before one selected layer, trained on 512 calibration samples (C4 or MATH, 2048 tokens), 1000 'epochs' lr 1e-4, 4 h on 8 H800. Speed: HF transformers, bf16, 2x A800-80GB (NVLink 400 GB/s) or 2x H20-96GB, Mixtral-8x7B only; TTFT at 1k/2k/4k input tokens (1 output token), ITL with 256 new tokens, 100 repeats. Batch size not stated. No CPU, no offload, no llama.cpp/vLLM.

Decode gain only 1.09-1.13x even on GPU. Math/domain quality loss 6.4 points.
quality_loss: Table 3: -1.8 to -2.5 points avg on 8 zero-shot tasks (after Hook); Table 2: -6.4 points on GSM8K/Minerva (Mixtral, MATH-calibrated Hook); plain top-1 without Hook -4.9 (general) / -6.9 (domain).
ablation: Table 2 calibration set (C4 vs MATH); Table 4 dynamic-k routing with/without TLNLE; Fig 1 layer-range sweep. No ablation of speed vs k on a memory-bound system.
limitations: Authors: compensation shrinks as k approaches original; models over 141B not evaluated (DeepSeek-V3, Grok-1, Qwen3). Speedup measured only in HF transformers; authors expect more with vLLM/SGLang.
contradicts_our_findings: No contradiction; consistent with our 1.3x ceiling lift (their 1.09-1.13x decode at k 2->1 on GPU). Their Table 4 shows top-1-in-upper-layers costs only 1.1%, i.e. per-layer k allocation (not uniform k) is a cheaper way to cut k than our uniform 10->4 gate test.

title: Mixture Compressor for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs Gains More (MC / MC-MoE). Wei Huang*, Yue Liao*, Jianhui Liu, Ruifei He, Haoru Tan, Shiming Zhang, Hongsheng Li, Si Liu, Xiaojuan Qi (HKU, CUHK, Beihang). ICLR 2025 (v2, 22 Feb 2025)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B (49B total, 13B active, 32 blocks, 8 experts, top-2) and Mixtral-8x22B (141B/39B, 56 blocks). PMQ: mixed-precision GPTQ, per-expert bit-width 1-3 bits chosen by LP using activation frequency, routing weight and quantisation loss; calibrated on 128x2048 C4; non-MoE layers 4-bit. ODP: online dynamic pruning, expert 2 skipped for a token if w1/w0 < median threshold, protecting ~2% most important tokens (attention + L1-norm score). Compression on 2-4 A100-80GB. Speed (Table 4, 13, 14): 16-bit baseline on 2x A100 (8x7B) / 4x A100 (8x22B); quantised models on 1x A100 or 1x RTX 3090, HQQ dequant kernels. Table 13 batches 1/8/16, input 512-4096.

ODP adds -0.56 points, -12.6% activated bytes, +0.08x speed

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: ODP reduces activated parameters by about 15% (Table 4: 4.53->3.96 GB at 2.54-bit = 12.6%; 3.73->3.23 = 13.4%), with <1 point accuracy drop; it is activated-param reduction, not stored-size compression.

Only these two

why: 8-expert top-2 models on GPUs; the 1.6-1.9x speedup is dominated by quantisation vs a 16-bit 2-GPU baseline (PMQ alone 1.63x), ODP adds 0.08x; ODP prunes at most 1 of 2 experts for 15% of tokens, nothing like 10->4 of 512 experts; our baseline is already ~4.3-bit so the 16-bit comparison inflates the gain; the paper's GPTQ+HQQ kernels are CUDA. The mixed-precision-per-expert idea (more bits for frequently used experts) does transfer as a design, but its measured effect is on perplexity, not on NVMe bytes.
ablation: Yes: PMQ vs uniform bits (Fig 5/6, Table 3), token protection (Fig 7/8), ODP threshold (Table 12), token importance metrics (Table 11). None isolates NVMe/offload cost.
limitations: Not stated in a limitations section; compression experiments need 2-4 A100; training-free but calibration-dependent; only Mixtral.
contradicts_our_findings: No contradiction. Supports: at 2.05-bit quality drops 8.6 points, i.e. our '2-bit adds at most 0.06 over top-4 at 16/32 GB' speed result must be read together with a large quality cost (our OLMoE Q2_K +26% PPL is consistent in direction).

title: Delta Decompression for MoE-based LLMs Compression (D2-MoE). Hao Gu*, Wei Li*, Lujun Li*, Qiyuan Zhu, Mark Lee, Shengjie Sun, Wei Xue, Yike Guo (HKUST, Birmingham, AISpeech). ICML 2025
setup: Models: Mixtral-8x7B, DeepSeekMoE-16B-Base (64 experts), Phi-3.5-MoE (16 experts), Qwen2-57B-A14B (64 experts). Method: Fisher-weighted merge of experts into one shared base Wb per layer, delta_i = W_i - Wb compressed by truncation-aware SVD, base pruned by semi-dynamic structured pruning (half static, half per input batch). Training-free, 512 WikiText-2 calibration samples, A100 GPUs. Quality: 3 PPL sets + 7 zero-shot tasks. Speed: Mixtral-8x7B, batch size 64 (Table 4), baselines NAEE, MoE-I2, LoSparse; no FP16 uncompressed row in Table 4.

why: GPU batch 64 (compute-bound, the opposite of our batch-1 byte-bound regime); the speed table has no uncompressed baseline; compression ratios are against 16-bit weights while ours starts from ~4.3-bit Q4_K, so a 40-60% reduction of fp16 bytes is a ~2.3-3.1 bit-equivalent already reached by plain quantisation; quality loss is already -0.06 (40%) / -0.11 (60%) points avg; the base is a layer-wide Fisher merge, so every token reads the shared base (not per-expert delta only) which is compatible with 'read base once per layer' but the paper does not build that kernel. Decomposition needs backward passes (Fisher) so a 125B model would be costly.
ablation: Yes: merge methods (Table 5), compressor choices for base and delta (Table 6: truncation-aware SVD on delta 5.28 vs vanilla SVD 6.22, activation-aware SVD 5.91, pruning 5.74), calibration size/source (Tables 8-9), delta trimming (Fig 4), ShareV/MergeU (Table 11). Nothing about a streamed-from-disk or CPU path.
limitations: Authors: 'involves decomposition and pruning steps with some complexity'. No other limitation stated.
contradicts_our_findings: Consistent with our closed form (about 50% size at rank ~64; ~1.5x). Their Fig 2 claims delta weights have much higher singular-value energy retention than raw experts, i.e. residual energy of the delta is the quantity we left unmeasured; paper shows it in a figure only (no 10%-at-r=64 number). MoBE (below) argues the effective rank of real experts (95% energy) exceeds break-even rank, which is evidence against our 10%-residual-at-r=64 premise.

title: Sub-MoE: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert LLMs Compression via Subspace Expert Merging. Lujun Li, Qiyuan Zhu, Jiacheng Wang, Wei Li, Hao Gu, Sirui Han, Yike Guo (HKUST, XJTU, Birmingham). arXiv 29 Jun 2025 (also AAAI per search result)

Method: K-means clustering of experts by output cosine, joint SVD on concatenated experts in a group giving a shared U, frequency-weighted merge of V, optional intra-expert compression (dagger variant). Calibration 128x2048 WikiText-2. Eight H800 GPUs; Table 2 runtime is tokens/sec on 8x H800 (batch and sequence length not stated).

Retention for 25/50% is in the abstract; others derived from Table 1 by me too

why: It reduces the NUMBER of experts (merging) and stores shared U per cluster; GPU 8x H800, no memory-bound/offload scenario; 50% expert reduction already loses 13-23% accuracy; merged experts change which expert a token needs, so it does not give a rank-r residual per original expert as in our variant. Interesting side: shared-U-per-group with expert-specific V is a lossy relative of our shared-basis + residual.

limitations: Authors: needs calibration data; data-free left to future.
contradicts_our_findings: No. It reinforces that high compression of expert weights costs quality quickly.

title: MoBE: Mixture-of-Basis-Experts for Compressing MoE-based LLMs. Xiaodong Chen*, Mingming Ha, Zhenzhong Lan, Jing Zhang, Jianguo Li (Inclusion AI, Renmin Univ., Westlake). arXiv 7 Aug 2025 (alphaxiv result says ICLR 2026)
setup: Models: Ling-Lite-Chat, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507, Qwen3-235B-A22B-2507, DeepSeek-V3-0324 (671B), Kimi-K2-Instruct (1T, 384 experts). Each expert up/gate matrix W_i = A_i B_i with B_i = sum_j alpha_ij B_j over m shared basis matrices (activation f applied), learned by minimising reconstruction error (Adam lr 0.07, H100s, data-free); down matrix untouched. m=4 (small), 32 (Qwen3), 64 (V3), 128 (Kimi). MoBE-dagger reduces k to offset extra activated params (8->6). 15 benchmarks. Baselines D2-MoE (needs calibration; infeasible on big models) and MoLAE. No latency measured.

title: Effective MoE-based LLM Compression by Exploiting Heterogeneous Inter-Group Experts Routing Frequency and Information Density (RFID-MoE). Zhendong Mi, Yixiao Chen, Pu Zhao, Xiaodong Yu, Hao Wang, Yanzhi Wang, Shaoyi Huang (Stevens, Northeastern). Preprint dated 13 Feb 2026

why: In-place reconstruction (no storage saving, explicitly out of scope); only the 'weakest' fraction of experts is compressed (25-50% of experts), not a shared basis plus residual for all; no speed; different models; MMLU collapse at rank 256 of I=512 shows a half-rank approximation of half the experts is unusable on Qwen. Useful as an accuracy ceiling for low-rank-per-expert on a 256-expert top-8 model: ranks near 50% of the intermediate dimension are needed even for 25% of experts.
quality_loss: See numbers; Qwen MMLU -3.6 (25%, r=128) to chance (50%); Gemma MMLU chat -2.8 (25%, r=176) to -19.7 (50%, r=88); GSM8K small changes.
ablation: Plain vs activation-aware vs mean-baseline SVD, rank, expert fraction (README tables). No storage/speed ablation.
limitations: README: memory saving needs factors stored separately and a changed forward pass (out of scope); results marked 'eval' still running; MMLU protocol depends on BOS handling for Gemma.
contradicts_our_findings: Supports the screen's warning that 50%+ compression of expert weights costs quality and that rank must be a large fraction of min dimension (Qwen I=512: rank 128 at 25% fraction loses 3.6 MMLU; rank 256 at 50% fraction loses everything).
